articles.title: Aurora Reports
articles.summary: This document compiles aurora reports from November 5, 2001, detailing observations of reddish and bright red glows in California (Union City, San Jose) and the Wisconsin/Minnesota border, noting the unusual visibility so far south. It also includes the San Jose Astronomical Association's activities calendar for December 2001 and January 2002, featuring star parties, meetings, and deep-sky observing dates.

articles.title: Our Aussie Outback Meteor Diary
articles.summary: The article chronicles Jane Houston Jones's journey to Alice Springs, Australia, for the 2001 Leonid Multi-instrument Aircraft Campaign. It details the team's arrival, search for a suitable dark sky observing site, and preparations for the Leonid meteor shower, including initial sky observations. The document also includes an unrelated travel account of Upheaval Crater and general astronomical observing notes for the upcoming month covering planets and lunar occultations.

articles.title: Minuteman Launch — 10 November 2001
articles.summary: A Minuteman launch was photographed on November 10, 2001, from near Castle Rock State Park, capturing its trajectory through the constellations Eridanus and Fornax. The article details the photographic conditions, including a last-quarter Moon, thin fog, and the use of a Tokina 28-85mm lens with 800-speed Kodak MAX film for a 4-minute exposure.

articles.title: Upheaval
articles.summary: Dave North recounts his challenging but successful second attempt with Akkana to hike into Upheaval Dome in Canyonlands National Park, a place he champions as the world's most spectacular impact crater remnant. They navigated a demanding "Black Diamond" off-road route and a sandy wash trail to explore the crater's "alien, unreal landscape," witnessing firsthand the profound geological evidence of a massive impact event.

articles.title: Holiday Planet Watching
articles.summary: This article highlights several celestial events for holiday planet watchers in late 2001, including a partial solar eclipse on December 14th, a near-occultation of Saturn by the Moon on November 30th, and a full occultation of Saturn on December 28th. It also mentions ongoing observations of sunspots and a new red spot on Jupiter. The author provides viewing tips and notes on local visibility for San Jose, California.

articles.title: Sports Weary Observer Reports
articles.summary: This article features an observer's report detailing late-night astronomical observations after watching sports. The observer, Bill Arnett, describes views of Saturn (including a glimpse of Enceladus), Jupiter (noting a Ganymede transit as a dark spot and a faint Great Red Spot), and the Moon (rilles, Apollo 11 trio), along with a humorous raccoon encounter. Separately, Gary Mitchell reports that the SJAA raised $271.50 from a flea market, including commissions and a donated telescope.

articles.title: San Benito County Passes Lighting Ordinance
articles.summary: San Benito County's board of supervisors unanimously approved a lighting ordinance on November 6th, culminating six months of collaboration and years of public outreach by Pinnacles National Monument and Fremont Peak Observatory Association. Modeled after Flagstaff's ordinance, it establishes three night sky protection zones around Pinnacles National Monument and Fremont Peak State Park. This move is now prompting incorporated areas of the county to draft their own lighting ordinances.

articles.title: Amateur Telescope Making Class Starting in February
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting an Amateur Telescope Making (ATM) class, focusing on mirror making, starting in February under the instruction of Tom Whittum at Houge Park. The class will meet bi-monthly, offering talks and grinding sessions, with a Foucault tester available for mirror figuring. Participants can bring partially completed mirrors, order new kits with a group discount, or work on a club-funded 'Community Mirror'.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: This document outlines the current status of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) telescope loaner program, detailing which telescopes are available for immediate loan, which are currently on loan with due dates, and those with extended loan periods. SJAA members can contact Mike Koop to borrow a scope, with instructions provided for pick-up, waiting lists, and transferring extended loans. The article also includes a note about needing storage space for telescopes.
